title: Kadison's similarity problem
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: Kadison's similarity problem, solved: every bounded unital homomorphism of a unital C*-algebra into the bounded operators on a Hilbert space is similar to a *-homomorphism (OpenAI, 2026). Completely bounded homomorphisms and Paulsen's similarity theorem; implementation of derivations with half the completely bounded norm and Arveson's distance formula; the noncommutative little Grothendieck inequality, row and column estimates, finitely generated homomorphisms and cyclic domains; Kirchberg's passage from inner derivations to similarity with a polynomial bound; words in free subalgebras; Schur-Weyl invariants, propagation from small corners and a Hankel test, which give a free-product corner estimate independent of the corner; transfer to II_1 factors through Popa's free independence in ultrapowers; the uniform commutator estimate for all von Neumann algebras; inner derivations, the similarity theorem with the bound ||pi||_cb <= ||pi||^(2C), and universal hyperreflexivity of von Neumann algebras.
prerequisites: OA-APPROX lessons completely-bounded-extension (Theorem 4.1: factorization of completely bounded maps) and sharp-noncommutative-bilinear-inequality (Theorem 1.1: Haagerup's noncommutative Grothendieck inequality; Section 4: three-lines bound (9))

foundations-of-von-neumann-algebras lessons on C*-algebras (Theorem 4.2, Proposition 7.3, Corollary 15.4, Proposition 17.1), Kaplansky's density theorem (Theorem 7.1), projections and types (Theorem 5.5, Corollaries 7.3, 10.4, 13.5, Propositions 4.3, 8.4, 14.2, 18.2) and the spectral theorem (Proposition 2.1, Theorem 3.1)
traces-and-noncommutative-integration lesson integration-for-a-trace (Theorem 1.1 duality, Theorem 3.1 commutation theorem, Theorem 9.1 trace-preserving conditional expectations)

generators-of-ii1-factors lessons haar-unitaries-freeness-and-ultraproducts (Section 1, Definition 2.1, Lemma 2.3, Corollary 2.4, Section 4 with Lemmas 4.1-4.2) and free-independence-in-ultraproducts (Theorem 4.2: Popa's free independence)

checks.exact_checks: numpy/scipy (scratch sim_checks.py, 8 Oct 2026), 37 checks: the norm beta(s) of [[1,s],[0,1]] and the limit (beta(cD)^2-1)/(2c) -> D/2 of the implementation bound; ||[x,p]|| = max(||b||,||c||) for block operators (Arveson's formula for a projection); the idempotent bounds beta(2s) <= ||pi_s|| <= beta(s)^2; the factorization x = (xx*+eps)^(1/2) v with ||v|| <= 1; the row estimate ||phi_{1,n}(x)|| <= sqrt2 ||phi||^2 ||x|| on 40 random similarities of matrix algebras (worst ratio 0.36 with ||phi|| underestimated); the three-lines bound ||ta-at|| <= log max(||e^-t a e^t||, ||e^-t a* e^t||) on 300 random pairs (worst ratio 0.9996) and its equality case; the integral int_0^1 c^tau dtau; the evaluation of cycle-trace forms on matrix units for p = 2, 3, 4; the equality of the spans of u^(x)p and g^(x)p (ranks 10, 20, 45); the vanishing antisymmetrizer on (C^2)^(x)3; orthonormality of (v^n+v^-n)/sqrt2; the narrow-arc Hankel data for N = 2..80 (entries >= 2 theta/pi^2 on the leading block, ||b||_2^2 <= u, min ||H|| pi^2 = 3.38 >= 1); Parseval for the arc function; Jordan's inequality; the Halmos symmetry on 50 samples; |x - 1_[1/2,inf)(x)| <= 2|x^2-x|; the map y(1+y*y)^(-1/2) and its inverse; the constants c1 = 699.58, Cfac = 2100.74, C = 6304.22; the layer-cake formula for a self-adjoint contraction; ||[T,e]|| = max of the off-diagonal blocks
